question: True or false: African wild dogs use sneezes to settle whether the pack sets off to hunt?
answer: True. Watching packs in Botswana, Walker and colleagues found that a rally ended in departure once enough dogs had sneezed. The number needed depended on who started it: when a dominant dog began, a few sneezes could do; a junior one needed many more. A sound usually filed as a reflex works as a ballot.
move: Before dismissing a signal as noise, check whether anyone acts on it.
trap: Assuming a sneeze is a reflex that cannot carry information.
source: Walker et al., Proc R Soc B, 2017
reference: Walker et al., Sneeze to leave: African wild dogs (Lycaon pictus) use variable quorum thresholds facilitated by sneezes in collective decisions, Proceedings of the Royal Society B, 2017
